JPG to PNG, PNG to JPG or PNG to WebP? How to Convert (and When Each One Makes Sense)

By the DoraPDF team · 5 min read · Updated 2026-11-12

Upload forms are picky. One portal wants JPG only, a design tool wants PNG, and a website speed test tells you to "serve images in next-gen formats". So you search convert PNG to JPG, or JPG to PNG online, and find a dozen converters that all look the same.

The conversion itself takes seconds. The useful part is knowing which conversion helps and which one just makes a bigger file. This guide covers DoraPDF's free image converters, what each one does under the hood, and a simple rule for choosing.

If you want the background on the formats themselves, our earlier guide JPG vs PNG vs WebP explains how each format stores an image. This one is the practical, "which button do I press" companion.

The converters at a glance

All of them work the same way: open the tool, drop your file(s), press the button, download. They run inside your browser, so your images are not uploaded to a server.

JPG to PNG: when it helps and when it does not

JPG and JPEG are the same format with two spellings, which is why the two tools behave identically. Both re-save your photo as a PNG, pixel for pixel.

Convert JPG to PNG when:

  • An app or upload form only accepts PNG.
  • You plan to edit the image several times. PNG is lossless, so saving it again and again does not add new blur or blocky artefacts the way repeated JPG saves can.
  • You want to cut out the background later. PNG supports transparency, so once your image is a PNG, a tool like the Background Remover can make parts of it see-through.

Do not expect:

  • Better quality. Converting cannot restore detail the JPG already threw away. The PNG looks the same as the JPG it came from.
  • A smaller file. A photo saved as PNG is usually larger, sometimes several times larger. That is normal.
  • Automatic transparency. A JPG has no transparent areas, so the PNG will not have any either until you remove a background.

You can add several JPGs at once and each one comes back as its own PNG.

PNG to JPG: the quick way to shrink screenshots and photos

PNG is great for screenshots, logos and text, but a phone photo saved as PNG can be huge. Converting to JPG is often the fastest way to get under an upload limit.

The PNG to JPG converter has a Quality slider (40 to 100, starting at 92). Lower numbers mean smaller files. For most photos, somewhere between 75 and 90 is hard to tell apart from the original on a screen.

One thing to know: JPG cannot store transparency, so any see-through areas in your PNG are filled with white. A logo on a transparent background becomes a logo on a white square. If you need the transparency, convert to WebP instead, or keep the PNG.

PNG to WebP: for websites and blogs

WebP is a modern format that most current browsers display. It can store transparency like PNG while often producing a much smaller file, which is why speed tools recommend it.

The PNG to WebP converter also has a quality slider. Transparent areas stay transparent. Use WebP for images on your own website or blog. For forms, email attachments or anything someone might open in older software, JPG or PNG is the safer choice, because not every program opens WebP files.

PDF to PNG and PNG to PDF

These two go in opposite directions and are handy for documents.

PDF to PNG turns every page into a sharp image. Pick a quality level: Normal for screens, High for printing (the default), or Ultra when you need to zoom in on fine print. A multi-page PDF also gives you a single .zip with all the pages, so you do not have to download them one by one. PNG keeps text crisp, which makes it the right choice for slides, diagrams and pages with small writing. For photo-heavy pages where size matters more, try PDF to JPG.

PNG to PDF does the reverse: add one or more PNGs and each becomes a page, in the order you added them. You can choose Fit page to image, A4 or US Letter, and a margin. It is a neat way to turn a set of screenshots into one document for a teacher or a bug report.

Illustrator and OpenDocument files

Illustrator to PNG converts the first artboard of an .ai file into a high-resolution PNG. It works with files saved with PDF compatibility, which is Illustrator's default setting. If you see an error, open the file in Illustrator, choose Save As, and make sure "Create PDF Compatible File" is ticked.

ODF to JPG and ODF to PNG accept LibreOffice and OpenOffice files. They rebuild the text (headings and paragraphs) and embedded pictures onto clean A4-sized pages, one image per page. They do not reproduce the exact fonts and layout of the original, so treat the result as a readable snapshot rather than a pixel-perfect copy. If the file has no text or pictures to read, the tool falls back to the preview thumbnail saved inside it.

A simple rule for choosing

  • Photo, need small: JPG.
  • Screenshot, text, logo, or need transparency: PNG.
  • Image for your own website: WebP.
  • Several images that must travel together: one PDF.

Privacy

Every converter on this page runs in your browser. Your photos, documents and design files stay on your device and are not sent to DoraPDF's servers.

FAQ

Is converting JPG to PNG lossless? The conversion itself adds no new loss, but it cannot undo the compression already in the JPG. The PNG will look the same as the source.

Why is my PNG bigger than the JPG? PNG keeps every pixel exactly, which takes more space for photos. If size matters, keep the JPG or try WebP.

Why did my transparent PNG get a white background? You converted it to JPG, which has no transparency. Use PNG to WebP or keep it as PNG.

Can I convert many files at once? Yes. The JPG, JPEG, PNG and WebP converters accept multiple images in one go.
